references.text: The original description of the courtyard hangings, pillars, and bases that God gave Moses on Mount Sinai.
The fulfillment of the instructions for the courtyard hangings, where the craftsmen actually made the pillars, bases, and the gate curtain.
A summary of the courtyard hangings, pillars, and bases as part of the completed work on the tabernacle.
The Lord's command to Moses to set up the courtyard around the tabernacle and hang the curtain at the gate.
The actual raising of the courtyard around the tabernacle and the altar, and hanging the curtain at the courtyard gate.
The responsibility of the Gershonites for the hangings of the courtyard and the curtain for the entrance, as mentioned in Exodus 35:17.
The service duty of the Gershonites included the courtyard hangings and the curtain for the entrance.
It specifies the dimensions of the gate curtain mentioned in the source verse by stating the number of pillars and cubits.
It connects the building elements from the source verse to their specific liturgical function in the Levitical service.
It confirms that the bases for the gate and the courtyard were made according to the original instructions.
It specifies the dimensions of the hangings on the west side as part of those same original instructions.
It completes the description of the gate curtain by giving dimensions for the other side.
This is the direct instruction for the gate curtain that the source verse refers to.
It specifies the holy material requirements (silver and bronze) for the pillars and bases mentioned in the source verse.
